allowed.plain: One technical round; a live RFP-only event can later get an RFQ added (when the client allows it).

RFQ converted into an auction: quotes become opening bids, the RFQ is ended and locked.

A direct auction with no RFQ before it.

More than two stages when building on the screen ('+' is disabled at two).

rows.title: Technical round (RFP)
rows.plain: Vendors answer the buyer's questions and upload documents; evaluators score the answers. Uses a technical (rfi) template. Position in an event: 1 (earlier stages come first).

rows.title: Price quote round (RFQ)
rows.plain: Vendors quote a price per line item (they may revise until the end). Uses a pricing (trade) template. Position in an event: 2 (earlier stages come first).

rows.title: Auction
rows.plain: Vendors bid live against each other and see their rank or the best price; the price keeps moving until the auction ends. Position in an event: 3 (earlier stages come first).

rows.title: Auction made from an RFQ
rows.plain: The RFQ's quotes become the starting bids of an auction; the RFQ is ended and locked. Position in an event: 4 (earlier stages come first).

rows.title: Which unit a line item ends up with, and when it is refused
rows.plain: On the screen the unit list is every unit of the client (from the settings payload), and picking a product pre-selects the product's FIRST linked unit. The server lower-cases it and looks it up among the client's units: the client's own units, plus Procol-wide units unless material codification or company-only units is on. A product linked to a unit that belongs to ANOTHER company (product_units is not filtered by company) therefore fails as soon as that unit is pre-selected, unless the buyer changes it to one of the client's units.
